operations.evidence: The Police workforce, England and Wales: 31 March 2026 bulletin was published on 22 July 2026.
Publication timing does not make national workforce data a parcel-level safety measure.

The bulletin covers the 43 territorial police forces in England and Wales; British Transport Police and National Crime Agency figures are supplied separately and are largely excluded from the England and Wales headline totals.
Coverage and counting boundaries must be retained when comparing totals.
There were 234,441 FTE paid police workers in the 43 territorial forces at 31 March 2026, down 1,332 FTE or 0.6% from the previous year.
A national workforce total does not establish local response capacity for an individual property.
There were 145,886 FTE police officers in the 43 territorial forces at 31 March 2026, down 566 FTE or 0.4% from the previous year.
Force deployment, demand and geography prevent direct conversion of the national total into parcel risk.
There were 20,989 FTE police officers and PCSOs in neighbourhood policing roles, 22.2% more than the 31 March 2025 baseline; 14,599 were officers and 6,390 were PCSOs.
The programme definition includes officers in training destined for neighbourhood roles and is not an exact local availability count.
There were 115,764 FTE officers in frontline roles, down 1.3% from the previous year; 90.5% of officers were recorded in frontline roles.
The frontline classification is functional and does not indicate patrol presence at a specific address.
There were 55,561 FTE officers in local policing roles, down 2,445 FTE or 4.2%; local policing accounted for 43.4% of officers.
Function-group totals are national aggregates and do not map directly to neighbourhood coverage.
There were 23,676 FTE officers in investigations and 15,298 FTE officers in public protection roles, representing 18.5% and 12.0% of officers respectively.
Functional staffing proportions do not measure incident probability or service quality at parcel level.
The national rate was 236 FTE officers per 100,000 residents; the Metropolitan Police Service had 347 and Lincolnshire 152 per 100,000.
Police-force-area population rates are not interchangeable with exact-address safety scores.
There were 7,259 FTE PCSOs at 31 March 2026, down 55 FTE or 0.8% from the previous year.
PCSO totals do not specify deployment, shift coverage or individual neighbourhood presence.
There were 5,196 special constables and 6,035 police support volunteers by headcount; the bulletin cautions that these figures can fluctuate when forces clean inactive records.
Headcount fluctuations and absence of contracted hours make these figures unsuitable for parcel-level capacity inference.
At 31 March 2026, 43,525 officers had less than five years of service, representing 29.4% of officers; 53.0% had less than ten years of service.
Length-of-service data are labelled Official Statistics rather than Accredited Official Statistics because of data-quality issues.
The Crime in England and Wales Quality and Methodology Information report was revised on 23 July 2026 and covers accredited official statistics and official statistics.
Statistical designation varies between component series and must not be applied uniformly.
The CSEW is a face-to-face survey of around 31,000 people aged 16 or over, while police recorded crime is an administrative count of notifiable crimes reported to and recorded by police.
Survey estimates and administrative records have different populations, error structures and uses.
The quarterly Crime in England and Wales bulletin uses the CSEW and police recorded crime as its two main data sources.
The two sources should be interpreted together but not treated as interchangeable measures.
The CSEW does not cover crimes against businesses, people not resident in households, homicide or offences often described as victimless such as drug possession.
Excluded crime types and populations cannot be inferred from CSEW household estimates.
